## Ruffster for Mac 0.1.24

Ruffster helps parents and children understand computer use together, including during the school day. This Mac family app keeps its monitoring status visible, encrypts activity reports for the parent, and includes a local dashboard. Setup shows which account it will monitor before monitoring begins.

### What changed

- The report's filtering guidance is shorter and easier to follow across home Wi-Fi, school Wi-Fi, and hotspots. It links to NextDNS as one setup example and advises families to ask before changing school-managed settings.
- The parent dashboard and encryption guide use plain language for family access and explain what reports can and can't tell you.
- The two-digit computer connection and report-sharing steps are unchanged.

Ruffster still records the app in front and network measurements, keeps its menu-bar status visible, and stores activity encrypted for the parent. It does not record screenshots, keystrokes, messages, audio, or camera data. The Mac app remains unsigned by Apple; follow the install guide's app-specific first-open steps and keep macOS protections on.

Automated Mac packaging and synthetic report checks passed. A real family setup and report exchange remain the next hands-on checks.

See the [family install guide](https://mikeymckay.github.io/ruffster/install.html), [privacy and children's rights notes](https://github.com/mikeymckay/ruffster/blob/main/PRIVACY-AND-CHILDREN.md), and the release's source commit.
